newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's SingTel to cut rates further in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's SingTel to cut rates further in 1997.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) said on Tuesday it would cut international direct dialling (IDD) rates further, by up to 46 percent to some destinations, from January 1, 1997.
A SingTel list of selected destinations including Indonesia, Japan, Taiwan, Britain and the United States, showed cuts of between 0.3 percent and 46 percent.

"This round of rate reductions will make our IDD rates even more competitive compared to incoming calls from these countries," Ng Seng Sum, SingTel's vice-president of international telecommunications service, said in a statement.
SingTel, which is 80-percent government owned, is due to lose its monopoly on basic domestic telecommunications services in April 2000. Some of its market has already been opened to competition.
SingTel has already cut IDD rates in January, April and September this year. In its last round of cuts, SingTel reduced IDD rates by up to 42 percent.
The company also plans to reduce rates for subscriber trunk dialling (STD) calls to east Malaysia and Penang and Ipoh in west Malaysia by up to 43 percent.
But it will raise the rate to the capital Kuala Lumpur by five cents a minute as part of its long-term plan to introduce a single rate for states north of Kuala Lumpur.
Ng said SingTel's revised IDD and STD rates would pass back to customers more than S$108 million (US$77 million) in savings over the next 12 months.
